q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 22, 2026. **4 days remain until the guidance is announced.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already provided official guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

This guidance was issued on May 20, 2026 (per the research provided). The question asks what the **forward guidance will be** in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release on August 26, 2026. 

Critically, the research confirms that NVIDIA's guidance assumes **no data center compute revenue from China**, which is a significant constraint on potential upside.

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will issue guidance in or near this $89.2–$92.8 billion range. While the research notes some analysts anticipate a "beat-and-raise" scenario similar to Q1 (where NVIDIA beat its $78.0B ±2% guidance with $81.6B actual), any raise would likely be modest—perhaps 3–5% higher than the current $91B midpoint.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Weaker demand signals**: If demand from customers has weakened since May, NVIDIA might lower guidance rather than maintain or raise it.
- **Supply chain issues**: Any manufacturing or logistics constraints could constrain available supply.
- **China restrictions tightening further**: If U.S. export controls tighten further beyond current assumptions, it could reduce available addressable market.
- **Macro deterioration**: Significant economic weakness could reduce enterprise capex spend.
- **Conservative posture**: NVIDIA might maintain conservative guidance to avoid missing targets.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Beat-and-raise pattern**: The research notes Q1 FY2027 exceeded guidance ($81.6B vs. $78.0B ±2%), and analysts anticipate similar for Q2. Strong demand signals and execution could justify a raise.
- **Stronger-than-expected demand**: If demand for H100/H200 GPUs and next-gen products remains robust, NVIDIA could raise.
- **Inventory absorption**: If customers are absorbing inventory faster than anticipated, demand visibility improves.
- **Supply improvements**: Better-than-expected supply availability could allow higher guidance.
- **China uncertainty resolution**: Any clarification that China restrictions won't worsen could unlock upside.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides:
- Q1 FY2027 guidance: $78.0B ±2% ($76.44B–$79.56B); actual: $81.6B
- Q2 FY2027 guidance (issued May 20): $91.0B ±2% ($89.2B–$92.8B)
- Q1 beat magnitude: ~$3.6B above midpoint, or ~4.6% above guidance
- Wall Street average: $91.9B (within guided range)
- Historical pattern suggests NVIDIA tends to guide conservatively and beat/raise

The $89.2B–$92.8B guidance range is already anchored on NVIDIA's own statement. The question is whether the company will maintain, lower, or raise this for the Q2 FY2027 earnings release on August 26.

---

## Reasoning on the 99.5–115.5 billion dollar range

The provided range extends well above NVIDIA's stated guidance:
- Lower bound: $99.5B is ~9.3% above the $91B midpoint
- Upper bound: $115.5B is ~27% above the $91B midpoint

Given that:
1. NVIDIA has **already provided** guidance of $91B ±2%
2. The research indicates this was issued on May 20, 2026
3. Wall Street consensus of $91.9B sits comfortably within the guided range
4. Even optimistic scenarios (beat-and-raise) typically produce 5–8% upside in mature, disciplined companies
5. The China restriction assumption limits upside

The probability of guidance landing significantly above $99.5B (8.4% above midpoint) is relatively low. However, NVIDIA's history of beating and raising, combined with strong demand signals, means modest upside toward $94–96B is plausible.

**Most likely forward guidance on August 26 will be in the $91–95 billion range**, with the midpoint near $92–93B (modest raise from $91B) or potentially a reaffirmation at $91B.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is expected to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings report on August 26, 2026. The company's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects Q2 FY2027 revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), meaning a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This guidance assumes no data center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, based on 42 estimates, have an average revenue forecast of $91.9 billion for the quarter [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This falls within NVIDIA's guided range. In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance of $78.0 billion (plus or minus 2%) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). Some analysts anticipate a similar "beat-and-raise" quarter for Q2 [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).
